STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel is a square flat plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no curved inner wall. Flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-sized, so about 24 cm.
b) Reference cue: almonds are 2.3 cm long. Across the plate's diagonal-free width (the plate spans roughly 420 px across, and an almond spans about 40-45 px), the width is roughly 9-10 almond lengths, so about 21-23 cm... The almonds are small relative to the plate, and the plate is clearly larger than a side plate. Reconciling the two cues, I take the width as about 23 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items (all on the plate, no sauce):
- Whole almonds: I count 14 visible (including one half-shell and one broken piece). Counting hidden pieces: the almonds lie mostly in a single layer, so add few hidden ones. Take about 15 whole-equivalent almonds.
  Grams = 15 x 1.2 g = 18 g.
- Almond fragments/shell pieces (the broken half-shell at upper right of centre and the piece at left) are mostly shell; count them as about 1 almond-equivalent extra. Total roughly 16 almond-equivalents, so 16 x 1.2 = 19 g.

Footprint check (cross-check by area): the almonds occupy about 10% of the 23 cm square (529 cm²) ≈ 50 cm², with a flat single-layer thickness of about 1.5 cm, giving ~75 ml x 0.5 (nut density, lower than 1.0 due to air gaps) ≈ 38 g, which is higher than the count method; the count method is more reliable for shelled nuts, so I use ~19 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No base layer or hidden food is visible under the almonds on the plate. None added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g: raw almonds are about 579 kcal/100 g.

Total: about 19 g of almonds, about 110 kcal.
